sentence: This project uses imaging to watch proteins and nucleic acids in live B cells as they improve and switch the type of their antibodies.
This project builds a toolkit of imaging and computer analysis methods to study how immune cells and their surroundings interact in solid tumors.
This project builds a technology to speed up the development of antibiotics that work against drug-resistant bacteria such as Escherichia coli.
This project studies how neurotensin circuits control dopamine neurons in the brain and affect reward-related behaviors, using genetic and imaging techniques.
This project builds three-dimensional human models of the blood-retina barrier that liquid can flow through, to study what goes wrong in retinal blood vessels.
This project provides mass spectrometry and computer methods to study proteins, metabolites and genome elements linked to aging.
This project studies how mitochondrial quality control works in the outflow facility of the eye and whether it causes ocular hypertension.
This project tries to find out how stem cells of the developing brain make the many kinds of nerve cells in the human cerebral cortex.
This project builds a microscope that uses sculpted light to stimulate and record the activity of many neurons in awake mice.
This project tries to find out how metabolic stress changes signaling in islet beta cells and leads to cell damage and diabetes.
This project tries to find out why the smooth chorion and the villous chorion develop differently in the human fetal membranes and placenta.
This project works to reduce illness and death from cancers of hormone-related tissues, such as breast, prostate and ovarian cancer.
This project tests whether lung cells grown from pluripotent stem cells can be transplanted into mice to restore airway and alveolar stem cell function.
This project studies where and for whom telehealth improves access to cancer care, and how its use affects outcomes in rural areas.
This project tests a survivorship care program in a randomized clinical trial to see if it improves quality of life for rural lung cancer survivors.
This project studies why zoonotic viruses stay harmless in animals such as bats and rodents but cause severe disease in humans.
This project builds computer tools and pipelines to process, combine and share large amounts of human virome data.
This project studies genetic, clinical, metabolic and socioeconomic data from children with cardiac arrest to understand what drives their risk.
This project uses gene therapy techniques to test how changing the tip link proteins in hair cells affects the current that carries sound signals.
This project tries to find gene variants linked to compulsive cocaine intake in rats and builds a shared repository of data and tissue.
